metadata.title: झूम खेत की रसोई में पका आदिवासी खाना | Gudok: A tasty and traditional dish of Tripura
metadata.description:
Gudok, a cherished delicacy from the picturesque state of Tripura, holds immense cultural and ethnic value among the tribal communities. This traditional dish is an integral part of ceremonial and community meals, celebrated for its unique flavors and connection to tribal heritage.

Prepared with love and shared with pride, Gudok is particularly popular among the Tripuri, Reang, and Mog communities. This semi-solid dish, made with fermented fish (locally known as berma), is a perfect blend of simplicity and tradition. It shares similarities with the Manipuri dish Eromba, as both rely on boiling an assortment of fresh vegetables in just the right amount of water and incorporating the tangy, umami taste of fermented fish.

In our special series, The Tribal Kitchen, we bring you an authentic Gudok recipe straight from the heart of Tripura's tribal areas. What makes this version truly special is the use of fresh, organic produce from Jhum (shifting cultivation) fields, ensuring every bite is a celebration of the region's agricultural practices and culinary traditions.

Stay tuned as we explore the rich flavors and stories behind Gudok, a dish that unites communities and carries the essence of Tripura’s tribal heritage!
